quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: If you are driving too slowly and traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Drive even slower.
Pull over to the right side of the road and let other cars pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.
Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right side of the road and let other cars pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. If traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane road, you must pull over and let cars pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: When should you not pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill.
In a curve in the road.
When you cannot see ahead clearly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills, in curves, or anywhere visibility is limited. Only pass when it is legal and safe to do so.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a driver wants to pass you, slow down. This gives them enough space to pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: Where must license plates be placed on a vehicle?

options.text: Only on the front.
Only on the back.
On both the front and back.
The driver can choose where to put them.

questions.correctAnswerText: On both the front and back.
questions.explanation: All vehicles must have license plates on both the front and rear. Any registered vehicle must display these plates to be parked or driven on a public road.

questions.question: Operating a motor vehicle is:

options.text: A privilege.
A right.
A requirement.
Simple.

questions.correctAnswerText: A privilege.
questions.explanation: Operating a motor vehicle is a privilege, not a right. If you misuse this privilege, your driver license can be suspended or revoked.

questions.question: What is an inattentive driver?

options.text: A driver who looks away from the road or daydreams.
A driver who stares at a passenger while talking.
A driver who only watches the car ahead.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, searching for items, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming. Always scan the road, check your mirrors, and look at your instrument panel regularly. These habits will help you stay focused while driving.

questions.question: What happens if a bicyclist does not obey traffic laws?

options.text: Bicyclists do not have to follow traffic laws.
They can receive a ticket.
Police will always give them a warning.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can receive a ticket.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights, duties, and responsibilities as drivers. Both motorists and bicyclists can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: What helps someone recover from drinking alcohol?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime.
Hot coffee.
Fresh air.
Only time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only time.
questions.explanation: Only the passage of time will reduce alcohol's effects on a person.

questions.question: What must drivers allow for when driving near heavy trucks?

options.text: Trucks need more time and distance to stop.
Trucks need less time and distance to stop.
Trucks make less noise.
Trucks travel faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Trucks need more time and distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Stay in areas where the truck driver can see you. Do not block the truck driver's view of traffic.

questions.question: What should you do when preparing to turn left?

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking your rearview mirror.
Move into the left lane.
Watch for oncoming cars and pedestrians.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal three to five seconds before turning left. Check your rearview mirror as you slowly reduce speed. On a multi-lane road, move to the left lane before the intersection. Yield to traffic and pedestrians, then turn when it is safe.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Grip the wheel tightly and slow down gradually.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the wheel tightly and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: If your tire blows out, do not brake suddenly. Hold the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas. Once you are going very slowly, apply the brakes gently and pull to the side of the road.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the road mean?

options.text: Drivers may make the movement shown by the arrow if they want to.
Drivers must make the movement shown by the arrow only if traffic lights are broken.
Drivers must always stop completely before making the movement shown by the arrow.
Drivers must make the movement shown by the arrow while obeying traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must make the movement shown by the arrow while obeying traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow painted on the road in your lane tells you that you must move in that direction. Always follow traffic signs and signals before moving in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid lines mean you cannot pass.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?

options.text: Service sign.
Regulatory sign.
Warning sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols or letters. They warn drivers about hazards or special situations ahead.

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your vehicle and others?

options.text: It prevents distractions from other vehicles.
It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
It keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
It keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Space between your vehicle and others gives you enough time to react if other drivers make mistakes.

questions.question: What should you do when a car ahead has blinding headlights?

options.text: Use your high beams until the other car dims theirs.
Flash your lights to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If another car's high beams blind you, look away from the headlights and toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This prevents you from being blinded.

questions.question: What should you do if you have a tire blowout?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas.
Do not use your brakes right away.
Slow down gradually and pull to the side of the road.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, take your foot off the gas and do not brake immediately. Slow down gradually, then gently apply the brakes and pull to the side of the road.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are also approaching.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and stop if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop, yield the right-of-way to other traffic, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the center line mean?

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass in your direction.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only alcohol above the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even a small amount of alcohol can
Only alcohol above 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even a small amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving skills will suffer. No one can drink and drive safely.

questions.question: When should you move back to your original lane after passing another car?

options.text: When you feel you are far enough ahead of the other car.
When the other driver signals you to move back.
When you are directly next to the other car.
When you can see the other car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the other car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back to the right lane when you can see the entire car you passed in your rearview mirror. Use your right turn signal before moving back to the right lane.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive when conditions are dangerous.
The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive when conditions are ideal.
The suggested speed to drive when conditions are ideal.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive when conditions are ideal.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed you can drive when conditions are ideal. You can drive slower than the posted speed, but you cannot drive faster. You must drive slower in school zones and work zones. If bad weather or road construction makes the posted speed unsafe, drive slower.

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Is always a very safe driver.
Always has the right-of-way.
Should not allow other cars to pass.
May create a dangerous situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous situation.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is hazardous. On a two-lane road with traffic backing up behind you, you must pull over and let other cars pass. Only drive much slower than the speed limit when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Lowers your blood alcohol level.
Cancels the effect of alcohol.
Does not change your blood alcohol level.
Raises your blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change your blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee does not lower your blood alcohol level. It may help you stay awake, but it cannot change how much alcohol is in your blood or make you sober.

questions.question: When driving at 60 mph, your field of vision is:

options.text: Two-thirds of what it is when stopped.
One-fifth of what it is when stopped.
Three-fifths of what it is when stopped.
Four-fifths of what it is when stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: One-fifth of what it is when stopped.
questions.explanation: As your speed increases, you can see less. At 60 mph, your field of vision is reduced to one-fifth of what it is when your car is stopped.

questions.question: You may park or stop on the freeway shoulder:

options.text: As long as you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your car is on the road.
If you need to check a map.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except in an emergency.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Do not pass.
Do not enter.
No turn on red.
Keep right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a divided highway is ahead. The road will split into two separate one-way roads with a median between them. You must stay to the right.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Steep downgrade.
Crossroad ahead.
No right turn.
Narrow bridge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings and alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down to avoid damaging your brakes or having an accident.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, it:

options.text: Slows your reaction time.
Makes you feel less confident.
Breaks down faster in your body.
Reduces driving mistakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reaction time.
questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, it slows your reactions, makes you feel more confident, and causes you to make more mistakes.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the other car.
You do not need to use a turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane only when you can see the front of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
